chunks: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whenever you come to water and there is little of it, sprinkle from your right and from your left and in front of you, and then perform wudu.'

key_terms.انْضَحْ: Sprinkle or splash water around; a purificatory act performed before using scarce water for wudu
key_terms.تَوَضَّأ: Perform wudu (ritual ablution); the prescribed Islamic act of purification before prayer
key_terms.قِلَّة: Scarcity or small quantity of water; a technical term in fiqh indicating the water is less than the threshold (kullatayn) required for automatic purification

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do when the available water for wudu is scarce according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) instructs that when water is scarce, one should first sprinkle water around the three sides — right, left, and in front — before performing wudu. This act of sprinkling (nadh) is understood in Islamic jurisprudence as a purificatory measure to remove any impurity that may have settled near the water source, ensuring the remaining water remains ritually pure for ablution. This ruling reflects the broader Shia fiqh concern with maintaining the ritual purity of small quantities of water.
